## Part 1 · 00:00

[00:00] There are a multitude of religions in the world, and these are all mutually contradictory with one another. Although college sophomores often like to say, "Well, they're all true." I think anyone who has really studied the world's religions understands that these cannot all be true because they make contradictory claims. Just compare Islam and Buddhism, for example.

[00:43] Islam asserts that there is a personal God who is omnipotent, omniscient, and holy, who created the world, uh that people are responsible to believe in him and perform good works that will merit salvation, and that after this life there awaits us either everlasting heaven or hell. Mhm. Buddhism believes none of these things.

[01:09] According to Buddhism, there is no personal God, the world is eternal, man does not have a soul which is distinct from the body, there is no such thing as heaven or hell or uh salvation, sin is illusory, um ultimately these beliefs have almost nothing in common, so they clearly cannot both be true. They could all be false, but they cannot all be true. So, that means that we have to face the difficult task of assessing what evidence and arguments can be offered on behalf of these various world religions.

[01:33] And I would argue that when it comes to Christianity, there are good reasons to believe, first of all, that there is a personal creator and designer of the universe who is the locus of moral values, who is distinct from the world and has made the world. And secondly, that this creator has revealed himself decisively in the person of Jesus of Nazareth, and has vindicated the radical personal claims of Jesus to stand in God's place to inaugurate the kingdom of God in human history by raising him from the dead.

[02:12] And so, on that basis, I think we can say that Christianity makes the best and most plausible claim to be the one true world religion.
